snip.t: Treat systemic disorders (e.g., iron chelation for haemochromatosis; corticosteroids/chemotherapy for amyloidosis or sarcoidosis).
Oral iron: known hypersensitivity to ferrous salts, active haemochromatosis.
Metabolic: Non‑alcoholic fatty liver disease (obesity, diabetes), haemochromatosis (rare)

Risk factors: chronic hepatitis B (about 200-fold risk, and HBV can cause HCC even without cirrhosis), hepatitis C, cirrhosis of any cause, alcohol, aflatoxin B1 (contaminated maize and groundnuts; the p53 codon 249 mutation), NAFLD/NASH, haemochromatosis.
snip.s: Liver tumours: benign, primary malignant and metastatic

qs.q: Which diagnostic blood parameter finding is characteristic of hereditary haemochromatosis due to iron overload?
qs.e: Haemochromatosis is characterized by high ferritin and transferrin saturation greater than 60%. Positive anti-mitochondrial antibodies are instead found in primary biliary cholangitis.
